newsitem.title: UK: Dlr/yen slips in Europe after Sakakibara comments.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/yen slips in Europe after Sakakibara comments.

text.p: The dollar was mixed at the European midsession, holding steady against the mark but edging lower against the yen along with mark/yen.

The yen perked up slightly after comments from senior Japanese Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara. In a speech to currency dealers in Tokyo earlier, he said Japanese authorities would intervene in forex markets when appropriate and when it can be effective.
He repeated comments he made overnight that recent yen moves were excessive and the market had taken too pessimistic a view of the Japanese economy, which he said was very healthy.

"Sakakibara keeps making these comments but he's using the intervention word more which is having some impact," said Teis Knuthsen, economist at First Chicago in London. "But there is still a deep-rooted skepticsm whether Japan will actually start intervening."
Dollar/yen, which held a tight range around 126 yen for much of the European morning session, eased to 125.87/97 at midday trade and down from late Tuesday's 126.23/33 yen.
Dollar/yen was also pressured by mark/yen's slip back below 73 after Sakakibara's comments which stood at 72.92/94 at the midsession but still above 72.84/86 yen Tuesday.

"The yen is overweak at the moment which, to an extent, is the Japanese authorities' fault," said Roger Francis, senior analyst at IBJ International. "Sakakibara can't say rates will go up without upsetting the markets, but he is saying the market should think about the future course of the economy."
The dollar ticked higher against the mark, largely due to mark/yen's decline, but did not stray far from European session ranges.
At midday trade, it stood at 1.7247/52 marks from 1.7318/23 late Tuesday in Europe and well-below Tuesday's fresh peak of 1.7375 marks.
Today's focus was on the U.S. March industrial production data due at 1315 GMT. An average of analysts' forecasts point to a 0.6 percent rise from the previous 0.5 percent rise.

In the wake of the benign CPI data on Tuesday which prompted a surge in U.S. stocks and bonds, analysts said a strong figure today could see U.S. rate hike speculation stoked up again. While this may have a negative impact on U.S. assets, dealers still see this as dollar supportive.
"The dollar seems to be in a win/win situation where strong data supports with rate hike speculation and weak data supports by stronger asset markets," said First Chicago's Knuthsen.
Elsewhere, the mark was steady on its European crosses while sterling was off earlier highs after UK data today came in below expectations.
UK February average earnings were in line with forecasts but January's data was revised downwards, cooling some of the recent speculation over higher UK rates.
Sterling/mark was weaker but off lows at the midsession, trading at 2.7985/95 marks from 2.8193/03 late Tuesday.
